--- title: "[Recipe.set_roles()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Return a new recipe with the given role assignments added. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/tidymodels/shoez/blob/examples-section/shoez/recipe.py#L191-L280){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Recipe.set_roles(*, outcome=None, predictor=None, case_weights=None, **custom) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Standard roles have dedicated keyword arguments; arbitrary custom roles may be passed as additional keywords. Each value is a column name or a list of names. Assignments are *added* to any roles the recipe already carries, so a column may end up with several roles at once; incompatible combinations (e.g. outcome + predictor on one column) are rejected. When the recipe was built with a prototype ``data`` frame, every name is checked against it; without a prototype there is nothing to check against, so any name is accepted and typos surface later, when the recipe is fitted. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [outcome]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | list[str] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Column(s) to assign the ``"outcome"`` role. Default ``None``. [predictor]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | list[str] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Column(s) to assign the ``"predictor"`` role. Default ``None``. [case_weights]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | list[str] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Column(s) to assign the ``"case_weights"`` role. Default ``None``. [**custom]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | list[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Any further keywords assign arbitrary custom roles, the keyword being the role name (e.g. ``group="city"``). The constructor's plural ``predictors=`` is rejected here rather than silently becoming a custom role. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Start from a frame whose columns need roles: ::: {#84268710 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} df = pd.DataFrame( { "price": [1.0, 2.0, 3.0], "sqft": [4.0, 5.0, 6.0], "city": ["a", "b", "a"], } ) df ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
price sqft city
0 1.0 4.0 a
1 2.0 5.0 b
2 3.0 6.0 a
``` ::: ::: Assigning roles returns a new recipe, leaving the original untouched: ::: {#9ab3e08f .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} recipe = Recipe(data=df).set_roles(outcome="price", predictor=["sqft", "city"]) recipe ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` Recipe (untrained) Inputs: 3 columns — 1 outcome, 2 predictors Steps: ``` ::: ::: Custom roles are just extra keywords, and stack with the roles a column already has: ::: {#7dc3ae6d .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} recipe.set_roles(group="city").roles.of("city") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` {'group', 'predictor'} ``` ::: :::
